chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Al-Harith ibn Hariz, from Sadeer Al-Sayrafi, from Abu Khalid Al-Kabuli, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he called for the midday meal, and I ate with him food that I had never eaten before, cleaner than it nor more delicious. When we had finished the meal, he said: 'O Abu Khalid, how did you find your food?' or he said: 'Our food?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have not seen anything more delicious than it, nor cleaner at all.'
But I remembered the Verse which is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'You shall certainly be questioned about the Bounties on that Day.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but rather you will be questioned about what you are upon from the Truth.'

key_terms.النَّعِيمِ: Bounties or favors (referring to worldly pleasures and blessings)
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: The Truth (referring to divine reality, faith, or adherence to truth)
key_terms.لَتُسْئَلُنَّ: You shall be questioned (future tense, indicating inevitable accountability)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific nature of accountability regarding worldly bounties according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between general accountability for material blessings (*al-na'im*) and the specific, primary accountability for upholding *al-Haqq* (Divine Truth and Imamate). It clarifies that while enjoyment of bounties is noted, the core of judgment lies in one's adherence to the truth during that enjoyment, a nuance often discussed in tafsir regarding Surah At-Takathur.
